## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.0-beta.7 automatically prepares memory updates for your review, sets up Gemma in the background, and bundles development workflows.

### Keep ordinary memories current

Threadnote now assesses eligible new and existing ordinary memories automatically. Within a bounded background budget, it gathers accessible current evidence and can prepare a private draft with your selected generation provider.

Library shows each assessment and its support, while Context Health lists prepared updates. Review the complete proposed body and its evidence before confirming Apply. Threadnote writes only the exact approved revision, verifies the canonical result, and preserves policy and historical paragraphs. Missing, partial, unavailable, or conflicting evidence stays visible instead of being treated as current.

Applying, rejecting, or deferring a draft remains an explicit choice. Shared and read-only memories keep their existing ownership and publication permissions. Advanced enrolled-topic workflows remain available for explicitly scoped maintenance.

Inspect or pause automatic drafting separately from the wider maintenance pause:

```sh
threadnote context maintain --action background-status --json
threadnote context maintain --action background-pause --json
threadnote context maintain --action background-resume --json
```

The default local budget is four generation units per rolling hour. Existing provider and model choices are preserved, and remote background use requires a separate finite grant.

### Prepare Gemma in the background

Eligible standalone installs and updates now download and verify the pinned Gemma 4 model in the background. Manager shows progress and recovery actions. Explicit provider and model choices stay intact; Gemma becomes the local default only when it is ready and you have not made a choice.

The download is approximately 4.6 GB, with memory and disk checks before it starts. Setup does not load the generation model or start a draft. Check progress with `threadnote models setup --status`, pause automatic setup with `threadnote models setup --auto off`, or retry with `threadnote models setup --retry`.

### Development workflows included

Threadnote now includes `dev-spec`, `dev-plan`, `dev-cycle`, and `watch-pr` for defining requirements, planning from current source, implementing and reviewing changes, and handling PR feedback. Supported agent setup installs them by default, and Threadnote updates refresh enabled installations while preserving edited files and opt-outs.

Use Manager's **Development workflows** page to preview and manage an installation, or start with `threadnote dev-skills list`. Installation makes the workflows available; it does not run them.

Development workflow setup handles changing Windows paths more reliably and preserves inaccessible or unowned files for review.

### Clearer reviews and memory previews

Memory and citation reviews have clearer evidence cards, quotations, status badges, and persistent actions. Maintenance review separates factual updates from policy conflicts and keeps protected history intact. Draft generation shows activity, uses current generation settings, and regenerates drafts when those settings change.

After acceptance, Manager confirms the saved update, closes the dialog, and clears the resolved item and its counts. Resolution persists after reload.

Memory conflict reviews keep Preview and Confirm visible. Choosing “Both memories apply” for shared memories saves a local decision for the reviewed versions without editing or publishing either source.

Memory previews now render Mermaid diagrams. Projects with display names containing spaces and topics with sentence-style filenames also work more consistently across review and maintenance.

### More reliable project-scoped context

Graph refreshes and recall preserve the selected project scope through scheduling and indexing. Temporary graph reference resolution can proceed while another SQLite connection holds the main writer, reducing busy failures during concurrent graph work.
